topic: MCP as an Observability Interface: Connecting AI Agents to Kernel Tracepoints

key_points: Original article framing MCP as an observability interface that connects AI agents to kernel tracepoints
Positioning MCP as the bridge between agent tool-calling and low-level kernel instrumentation
Note: page currently returns 404 (Page not found) — treat as the topic's origin/seed reference, not a live competitor
MCP-based architectures enable AI agents to invoke tools, but what happens in between is a black box
Latency spikes in tool responses (e.g. external API slowing down) degrade agent performance
Silent failures occur when a tool invocation does not return valid data
OpenTelemetry chosen for context propagation, multi-language support, and open standards
Observable signals: performance metrics, distributed tracing, tool_token_usage_total counter for cost tracking
Common failure modes: timeouts, connection errors, silent failures, token/cost overruns
The observability gap: infrastructure solved observability a decade ago (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog), but AI agents remain opaque
Traditional APM sees HTTP 200 and 143ms latency and calls it success, but misses: leaked PII, hallucinated citations, cost overruns, prompt injection
What's missing is protocol-native observability — most approaches are SDK-based instrumentation, not protocol-level
OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are now published, including dedicated specs for agent spans and MCP server telemetry
Cost visibility is a blind spot: agents make chains, not individual calls; a $0.01 API call becomes $0.50 per execution when you trace the full chain
Security is the adoption bottleneck: 25% of MCP servers have no authentication; 38% say security concerns block adoption
Every major observability vendor is adding agent capabilities (Datadog MCP bridge, Arize Phoenix on OTel GenAI conventions)
ClickStack MCP server allows external AI systems and agents to integrate directly with observability primitives
MCP for observability is about orchestration, not just investigation — agents drive the full incident workflow
Chat alone does not match how real incident investigations unfold; engineers jump between logs, traces, dashboards, deployments, hypotheses
Every query, chart, reasoning step, and intermediate result should be visible and auditable
MCP servers for observability may not be the holy grail it is hyped to be
LLMs are not yet ready to replace human SREs — hallucinations, misclassification biases, lack of explainability
No real world model: an LLM can give perfect directions on a map it was trained on but has no ground-truth model of the live system

Deviations and alignments: agent suggestions must be confirmed against dashboards/logs/traces; combinatorial explosion of tool chains means the agent can go astray unless aligned with ground truth at every step
Human-in-the-loop and careful constraints remain essential
Kernel observability via eBPF: attach programs to kprobes, uprobes, XDP packet ingress paths
Tracepoints, kprobes, uprobes are the static and dynamic instrumentation points in the Linux kernel
eBPF enables low-overhead, safe kernel-level observability without modifying kernel source
Linux kernel tracepoint challenges (2016 Kernel Summit, Jonathan Corbet)
Tracepoints are static instrumentation points in the kernel; maintaining stable tracepoint ABI is a known challenge
Tracepoints must be kept stable across kernel versions to avoid breaking tracing tools
